Project: Production RAG Chatbot (Confidential Client) — Grounded FastAPI chatbot with policy routing. Goal: Inherited a basic domain chatbot that answered loosely, missed edge cases (greetings, follow-ups, out-of-scope asks), and could not reliably capture leads. The job was to turn it into a production RAG system that stays grounded in approved knowledge, routes intents safely, validates quality before reply, and converts high-intent conversations into structured leads—without leaking proprietary product branding publicly. Outcome: ~45% fewer ungrounded / out-of-scope answers; ~35% higher relevance on regression scenario suites; ~30% better qualified lead completion; ~50% more failure modes caught pre-release via scenario + regression tests; ~40–50% faster iteration from requirement → hardened release using AI-assisted delivery. Approach: Replace “one prompt calls the model” with a modular orchestration loop owned by a FastAPI service: retrieve evidence from a vector store → classify conversational intent → generate a grounded answer (or controlled refusal/redirect) → run hard/soft validators → return typed ChatResponse with optional citations. Keep lead capture as a parallel state machine so sales collection never contaminates answer grounding. Cap session history and persist lead state per session id so multi-turn chat stays coherent and recoverable. Why this approach: Domain Q&A fails when answers are ungrounded or when edge intents share the same generation path as factual replies. Explicit routing is cheaper and more testable than hoping the LLM always behaves. Pre-response validation + a soft review queue catch policy/quality slips that pure prompting misses. Separating lead extraction from RAG generation keeps prompts focused and measurable. How built: Python FastAPI routers expose typed `/chat` contracts (`ChatRequest`/`ChatResponse`). Core logic lives in an orchestrator that loads/saves lead state under a session-safe path, appends capped history, and calls retrieval → generation → validation. Source display maps internal chunks to public citation labels. Frontend is React 19 + Vite + TypeScript with markdown rendering, axios API client, and content-safety utilities. Regression/scenario test suites exercise routing and retrieval. CI runs on GitLab. TTS batch utilities generate guided-page narration assets used by the UI. Evals: Scenario + retrieval regression suites for routing/grounding; soft-issue review queue for production drift; typed response statuses (`lead_submitted`, quality blocks, etc.) make offline analysis and UI branching deterministic. Tech: Python, FastAPI, RAG, Vector Search, Pydantic, React, Vite, TypeScript, TTS, Prompt Engineering, pytest, GitLab CI. Tags: AI, Full-Stack.

Project: TwinMind — Live transcription + suggestion agent. Goal: Build a live meeting copilot: capture audio in ~30s chunks, stream transcription word-by-word to the UI, generate exactly three typed suggestion cards per segment, and support grounded chat expand/continue with independent transcript windows. Outcome: Working FastAPI + Next.js system with NDJSON streaming transcription, schema-locked suggestion JSON (with retry without `response_format` when providers reject JSON mode), temperature-per-task controls, and Netlify-ready frontend + separate backend hosting. Approach: Split client/server responsibilities hard: browser owns MediaRecorder chunking, transcript identity (`rowId` vs `chunkId`), and settings; FastAPI owns all Groq calls (Whisper + chat) so keys never live in `NEXT_PUBLIC_*`. Use NDJSON streaming for transcription UX. Force suggestion outputs through schema-in-prompt + JSON mode. Keep suggestion rolling window and chat grounding window as independent minute settings. Why this approach: Meetings punish latency and unstructured model output. Chunk streaming feels real-time. Strict JSON keeps the three-card UI stable. Independent context windows prevent “chat history” from polluting per-chunk suggestions (and vice versa). Server-side LLM calls are the only responsible key-handling pattern for a demo that still looks production-shaped. How built: Monorepo: `frontend/` (Next.js 16, React, TypeScript, Tailwind) and `backend/` (FastAPI, pydantic models, httpx). Transcription streams paced word deltas after Whisper returns. Suggestions use temperature ~0.65 and JSON mode with a compatibility retry. Chat expand/continue use lower temps (~0.5 / ~0.55). Settings persist in `localStorage`. Netlify `base=frontend`; backend deployed separately with CORS for the site origin. Evals: Manual latency/feel checks on streaming; JSON parse resilience via retry; UI regressions around duplicate `chunkId` rows and SSR clock mismatch handled with client-only time rendering; export artifact used for end-to-end review. Tech: Next.js, TypeScript, FastAPI, Groq, Whisper, httpx, NDJSON Streaming, Prompt Engineering, Netlify. Tags: AI, Full-Stack.

Project: AlphaBot Trading System — Backtest → walk-forward → paper/live. Goal: Build an autonomous trading stack where research, walk-forward optimization, and live execution share one pipeline—so offline validation actually predicts production behavior—and live trading stays gated behind risk controls and an explicit cutover runbook. Outcome: Python 3.12 Conda environment with OHLCV parquet cache, walk-forward optimization (overfit flags when OOS Sharpe collapses vs IS), paper/live Alpaca adapters, portfolio guards, session restore, and LIVE_TRADING operational checklist. Approach: Architecture as a multi-agent / staged pipeline: market scan → signals → regime classification → confirmation → decision → risk/portfolio guards → broker execution → lifecycle tracking. Prefer local cached OHLCV for WFO grids (`cache_only` after prefetch) to avoid Yahoo rate limits. Run WFO on the same live pipeline code with mock sentiment during grids. Promote configs only after IS/OOS review. Why this approach: Trading ML dies from train/serve skew and silent overfit. Sharing the live pipeline in backtests is the reliability answer. Walk-forward is stricter than a single split. Caching makes Windows WFO practical. Kill-switches, confirmation gates, and paper-first execution exist because finance demos that skip ops controls are not “systems engineering.” How built: Installable Python package (`alphabot`) with `environment.yml` locked to 3.12 (Alpaca/aiohttp/PyYAML build constraints on Windows). YAML settings + `.env` secrets. pytest for WFO/live pipeline tests. Structured logging and decision stores for auditability. Documented live cutover (`CONFIRM_LIVE`, kill-switch drills, risk ramp). Evals: WFO JSON/Heatmap reports; overfit flag heuristic; pytest coverage on walk-forward live pipeline; paper trading before live keys; preflight validates Alpaca keys only when live mode is on. Tech: Python 3.12, pandas, yfinance, Alpaca, Walk-Forward Optimization, pytest, Conda, AsyncIO, Risk Management. Tags: AI, ML, Data.

Project: E-commerce RAG Agent — Clean → embed → Redis semantic search. Goal: Enable semantic product Q&A over noisy Amazon electronics FAQ/text by cleaning aggressively first, then retrieving with normalized MiniLM embeddings stored in Redis. Outcome: Batch ingestion with HTML/URL/email scrubbing, unicode normalization, dedupe, batch-32 embeddings (`all-MiniLM-L6-v2`), Redis JSON docs with vectors, and FastAPI API scaffold for phase-2 retrieval. Approach: Make retrieval a data-quality problem first. Clean every text field (HTML tags, entities, URLs, emails, special chars, unicode), drop empties/dupes, concatenate fields per row, embed with normalized MiniLM vectors, and store in Redis under prefixed keys for cosine similarity search. Why this approach: Retail text is hostile to embeddings when HTML/noise remains. MiniLM (384-d, ~80MB) is the right speed/quality tradeoff for FAQ search. Redis is an easy online store for demos without standing up a full vector DB cluster. How built: Python ingestion script with explicit cleaning helpers, Redis client load path, `.env` for HF/Redis/CSV config, docker-compose for Redis, and requirements locking torch/sentence-transformers/onnx runtime style deps for local runs. Evals: Count deltas logged at each cleaning stage; Redis ping + batch load progress; manual semantic spot checks on product questions after ingestion. Tech: Python, sentence-transformers, ONNX, Redis, Docker Compose, FastAPI, ETL, NumPy. Tags: AI, Data.

Components: **Ingestion service** — cleaning + embedding + Redis load | **SentenceTransformer MiniLM** — HF auth via env token | **docker-compose Redis** — local vector/doc store | **FastAPI scaffold** — API surface for retrieval phase.

Project: MarketCanvas-Env (RL + MCP) — Semantic canvas env for banner layout agents. Goal: Build a deterministic Mini-Canva style environment where RL policies and LLM/MCP agents learn marketing-banner layout under explicit prompt constraints (headline, CTA, contrast), with bounded rewards that resist trivial hacking. Outcome: Gym-style env with semantic JSON observations, high-level actions, dense/terminal reward modes, WCAG contrast term (>=4.5), anti-duplication penalties, MCP tool interface, and a writeup covering PPO scaling to ~10k VLM rollouts. Approach: Prefer semantic actions (add/move/recolor) and JSON state (bbox, colors, overlaps, centering flags) over pixel mouse control early. Shape reward as weighted constraints (0.40) + aesthetics (0.25) + accessibility (0.25) + anti-hacking (0.10). Expose MCP for interactive agents while keeping direct Gym stepping for training throughput. Why this approach: Early RL learns faster with smaller action spaces and interpretable state. Keyword gaming still exists, but duplication penalties block the cheapest exploits. Dual MCP/Gym interfaces separate demo interoperability from actor-learner training paths. How built: Python packages for observation/action/reward/canvas env, optional PIL RGB renderer for multimodal experiments, MCP tool responses for agent tooling, and a detailed writeup on vectorizing envs / observation tiering for large parallel VLM rollouts. Evals: Reward bounded in [-1, 1]; known loopholes documented (keyword gaming, alignment inflation); anti-dupe tanh saturation tested conceptually against identical CTA spam. Tech: Python, Reinforcement Learning, MCP, Gym API, Reward Design, PIL. Tags: AI, ML.

Project: Pink Slime Journalism Analysis — NLP clustering of misinformation style. Goal: Find linguistic/stylistic signatures that separate pink-slime journalism from legitimate news. Outcome: Analyzed 27k+ labeled sentences; pink slime showed oversimplified language and ~3× sentiment exaggeration patterns. Approach: Vectorize text, score sentiment/readability, reduce with PCA, cluster with K-Means, and extract cluster signatures for downstream classifiers. Why this approach: Misinformation style is multi-feature. Unsupervised structure discovery surfaces patterns before committing to a supervised label model, and is auditable for research. How built: Python NLP stack (tokenization, TF-IDF/embeddings, sentiment tools), PCA + clustering, and reporting of category-wise stylistic divergence across Politics/Business/Health. Evals: Observed ~3× sentiment exaggeration patterns in pink slime vs legitimate journalism; cluster interpretability reviewed qualitatively across topic categories. Tech: Python, NLP, PCA, K-Means, Sentiment Analysis, TF-IDF. Tags: AI, ML, Data.
